newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgarian Inv Bank has 723 mln levs '96 net profit.
newsitem.headline: Bulgarian Inv Bank has 723 mln levs '96 net profit.

text.p: The private Bulgarian Investment Bank (BIB) posted 722.5 million levs net profit for 1996 under local accountancy standards, up from 13.16 million levs the year before, a bank official said.
"The bank posted a net profit of 722.5 million levs for last year and the shareholders decided to transfer it to the bank's reserves," the bank's legal adviser Teodora Shipkova told Reuters.
Under international standards the bank's net profit for 1996 totalled 1.7 billion levs, Shipkova said. Its net profit for 1995 was 10.65 million levs by those standards.

BIB was set up in 1994 as the first investment project of the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) in Bulgaria's banking sector. The EBRD now holds 35 percent of the bank's capital.

The shareholders on Thursday decided to admit a new shareholder to contribute to a capital rise to 2.2 billion levs, the minimum required now for a full banking licence, Shipkova said, declining to elaborate.
Last year Bulgaria's central bank allowed BIB, which has been licensed for domestic operations alone, to operate abroad through correspondent accounts.
The central bank said BIB would be granted a full banking licence when the 2.2 billion lev minimum capital was paid-in.
The bank's paid-in capital totalled 800 million levs as of December 30, 1996, figures showed.
